steps.content: Late at night, at the Central Library.

A car pulls up quietly at the entrance. A woman steps out and passes the security scan. The door opens. Alone, she climbs the white stone steps, enters the silent corridors, and makes her way deep inside, toward that familiar window.
Celine has just returned from a private banquet in Paradeisos. She's on the phone with someone.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You're giving me too much credit. My words certainly don't wield that kind of influence. It's all simply the natural course of the times.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Yes, that's right. And thank you for your support as well. I still have some work to wrap up here. We'll be in touch.
Finally, it's over. Celine retrieves her book, picks up her pen, and prepares to record the day's findings. Just then... she senses something unfamiliar.
In the silence of the night, she is not alone in the library.
She smiles faintly, tidies her things, and settles into her seat.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: "I can sense it through the shackles." ...Come on out, Chief. Come sit with me.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You came here alone at this hour. It must be something quite important, I imagine.
She says her greeting toward the shadowy corner.
So you come out, stopping roughly seven steps in front of her.

options: Someone suspects you're a spy sent to infiltrate BR-003.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You had two lines of contact. You reached out to Lemma early on, and later, to me. Combined with the exceptionally high clearance you already held, if that really was your plan, you certainly had the means to carry it out.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So I reported it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But the investigation ruled out that possibility. Someone higher up vouched for you. The evidence that person provided was apparently more convincing. It proved... you weren't working for the Underground.
The sound of flowing water dissolves the icy air. The atmosphere seems to ease up a little.
Yet the visitor's face is still hidden in the shadows.
You toss several books onto the long desk between you. They slide across the polished surface. Three hardcovers and one printed manuscript.

The light is dim, but Celine sees it clearly. A book series titled: <color=#fb9259>Rust and Blood: Tracing the Origins of the Syndicate Riots</color>. The cover image is set against a ruin near the Rust. A mobster grips a Mania weapon, bloodshot eyes staring viciously into the camera. The hatred and madness feel almost visceral, jarring.

Even more jarring is the weighty author byline:
<color=#fb9259>United Humanities Society</color>.
You stop beating around the bush.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "I have a new book coming out, and it urgently needs proofreading." This is the book you were talking about?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I did compile it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This book presents itself as an objective academic analysis, but every line is designed to persuade the reader of something. It deliberately magnifies Rustfire's violence while glossing over their hardships and determination.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It also cites a lot of sources to frame the mining disaster as an "unfortunate accident." It emphasizes Nirvana's apology, portraying the corporation as the innocent victim. And in the end, it points toward the resistance against the current mine development... What kind of conclusion are you trying to draw?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A chronicler cannot possibly be ignorant of the truth. How could you write something like this?
She remains in her usual spot, leisurely flipping through those books while responding to your questions patiently, just like before.
...She won't even use the name "West District."

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Because people still need it.</color>

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: My research may not directly advance society the way Lemma's does, but my field has its own strengths.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: News, commentary, literature, and even these historical writings of mine. They are all crafts in their own right. Our specialty lies in presenting ideas, shaping narratives through writing and multimedia, and ensuring they reach as many people as possible.
Her hand glides over that truth-distorting cover photo, tapping it twice approvingly.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: See, truth isn't simply recorded and unearthed. It can also be subtly reshaped through our work, quietly remolding how people perceive the world. That's an ability modern society needs now more than ever.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: That's precisely why, while the College of Humanities may not enjoy the spotlight the way the College of Science does, we still receive steady funding from a variety of sources. My sponsor likely entrusted this project to me because...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: They found my writing rich in detail, emotionally compelling, and persuasive.
She smiles.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: And I've cultivated quite a respectable reputation too. "Noble," "dignified," "dedicated to scholarship." I've always been careful not to leave traces that might tarnish that image... That makes readers far more inclined to "trust" me.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: After all, my sponsor prefers to keep this deal discreet.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The whistleblower who exposed all this had her account banned. Both the Public Security Bureau and the Underground raided her home. Were you aware of that?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I am aware now. Thank you for telling me.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: That student has a really unique perspective. I check her site often, and I've always worried about her. Getting that deep into sensitive topics, and being so blunt about them—it's only a matter of time before she catches attention. From a lot of people.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: No need. Not worth it. And don't worry. Pixel's been through this before. She knows who's behind it, and she'll get out of it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You seem to know your sponsor quite well. You must have worked with them far longer, and far more closely, than you ever did with me. Do tell me more, then.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Out of the four latest Black Ring ruin incidents, the BR-002 mine was hit the hardest, with an ever-growing casualty count. The Underground had no motive to do this. It served none of their core interests. But damage to Rustfire does benefit another group...

options: What's the connection between your sponsor and the Sillage Society?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I can't disclose that. For now, I still need their "trust."
<color=#fb9259>"Trust"</color>?
The word, spoken aloud, feels laughable. You yourself are laughable too, perhaps.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You once said...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But for me, the greatest reward was crossing that divide between East and West. Walking down streets I'd only ever seen in photographs. Meeting the people who actually live there. At first, they were wary of a "Paradeisos scholar" like me, and curious, too. But by the end of each conversation... every one of them shook my hand.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You knew the truth wasn't like what you wrote in your book. You went there yourself. You met the people. You saw with your own eyes how much they sacrificed for that mine. You experienced it firsthand.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Words, in the end, can only hold fragments. The real history has settled into every brick and stone of West District, into the people whose lives are woven into that place. When they opened their hearts to me... that's when I truly saw the marks time had left behind. And the light still shining through them, too...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And what about their trust? Did it mean so little to you that you could simply throw it away?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did you get me to connect you with West District so you could keep working on this pack of lies you call your "book"?
Some questions answer themselves the moment you ask them. Whatever she says no longer matters.
Yet she still meets your eyes, still smiling, and answers anyway.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Yes, thank you for setting that up.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I had to gather rich, authentic details, which I could then filter, refine, and reassemble. That's how I instill "credibility" in my works.
A deathly silence fills the library. Only the high-mounted clocks' pendulums tick in the stillness. Now, in the quiet of the night, you finally hear it...
The clocks are out of sync. Their chimes narrowly miss each other, the discordant sounds making you uneasy.
Celine watches you, the night melting into her deep blue eyes.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: To climb the ladder of the system. To penetrate the deeper, hidden layers.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: My pen bought me entry into their world.
She gently turns the pages in her hands.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Generations of chroniclers inherited the pages left behind by those before them. They did all they could to record history and the times they lived in, piecing together fragments of truth, then passing it forward. And to obtain this precious fruit, one must always pay a price.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: And so my predecessors staked their wealth, reputation, information, and time... Some even wagered their freedom and lives. I've inherited many invaluable findings, but I've also witnessed a frustrating truth. Even after sacrificing so much, they never received the rewards they deserved.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Because they couldn't let go of their "conscience," Chief.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Truth isn't locked away in ivory towers, nor does it rest solely in virtuous hands. It's woven into every corner of society.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You once told me that one must see clearly what one wants in order to move forward. I understand what you want now, but Celine...

options: Isn't there a line you won't cross?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This entire series was written to pressure the mine workers into backing down. You're twisting their persistence into something else. You're not just recording history. You're tainting it.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: An era shapes its chroniclers. To record the truth, you must breathe it.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: So I traded away a few "principles" in exchange for some admission tickets. The same way I borrowed your precious trust to gain entry into West District.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I've indeed gained a lot. I'll need some time to sort through it all.
She looks at you and smiles. The night, you realize, is cold.
Dazed, you find yourself with nothing left to say.
...One last question.

options: What about Linda? Does she know?

steps.content: Celine's smile deepens.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: She's my chosen successor. Sooner or later, she'll walk the same path.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Chief, our deal is still valid. Don't forget that.
She sets down the book, rises, and walks toward you.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: The Sillage Society, and the Underground, right? The truth you're looking for may come to light very soon. So... will you wait for me just a little longer?
Celine Fabius stops before you and looks up with a smile. She's waiting, as if she's just posed a question to a "student," or daring an opponent to make the next move.
steps.female_content: Celine Fabius stops before you with a smile, her eyes level with yours. She's waiting, as if she's just posed a question to a "student," or daring an opponent to make the next move.

steps.content: You don't actually need to give her a response. She's most likely unrelated to the leak, and the two of you will probably never walk the same path again.
But... perhaps this moment is exactly why you came to meet her tonight.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Since the moment I decided to face the Black Rings head-on, I've had to rely on the help of the brightest minds. And there was a time when I truly needed all of you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Like many in this city, we believe in logic and reason—the fruits of our civilization. We also believe in those who have reached the pinnacle of rationality, who dedicate themselves to the pursuit of truth and knowledge.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Just as I believe humanity can overcome Mania, I want to... believe in all of you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Give me the true answer, Professor.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I want to understand why someone who would stop at nothing to achieve her goals, someone who claims to have cast aside her own "conscience," would still choose to face me with honesty.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The battle of BR-003 isn't over yet. I am accountable to the people I've made promises to, and I need to eliminate every risk. Until this all comes to an end, until you tell me the truth, I won't be telling you anything more.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But when this is all over...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: When that time comes, I'll be waiting for your answer, and that part of your "conscience" you haven't sold.
Celine stares at you intently. Slowly, her smile melts into something softer.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: ...Thank you, Chief. That's exactly what I needed to hear. Let's talk more when you return.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Look at me. See right through me. I know you must be able to see it clearly.
Jump

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Since the moment I decided to face the Black Rings head-on, I've had to rely on the help of the brightest minds. And there was a time when I truly needed all of you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Like many in this city, we believe in logic and reason—the fruits of our civilization. We also believe in those who have reached the pinnacle of rationality, who dedicate themselves to the pursuit of truth and knowledge.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Just as I believe humanity can overcome Mania, I want to... believe in all of you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But rationality seems more complicated than I thought. People like you, who stand at its pinnacle, are far beyond my reach. I can't see you clearly anymore, and I don't have the strength to keep trying.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The battle of BR-003 isn't over yet. I am accountable to the people I've made promises to, and I need to eliminate every risk. Until this all comes to an end, until you tell me the truth, I won't be telling you anything more.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I won't treat you as an enemy, not until I have solid evidence.

options: But I won't regard you as a friend anymore either.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The toughest battlefield still lies ahead. I can't rely on someone I don't trust.
Celine stares at you intently. For a moment, you can't tell whether the expression on her face is a smile or something else. Then you hear her speak, softly.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: It's alright, Chief. You were too kind to me before. Let's take this chance to get to know each other all over again.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Look at me. See right through me. I much prefer the way you look at me now.
end

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: The history I record can only reach the truth through eyes like yours.
She raises her hand and touches your eyes, as if also touching what they scrutinize—herself.
[Black Screen]
She sees the guest out and shuts out all the noise. It's time to focus on her research. As the library begins its closing procedures, she prepares to return to the silence of history.
Yet, footsteps echo through the empty library once more.
[Return to background]
Celine recognizes whose footsteps these are. She lifts her head and recovers her smile.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: What brings you here? Your thesis has been accepted. You don't need to burn the midnight oil anymore. You should be getting some proper rest.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Or did you come to celebrate with me?

steps.speaker: Linda
steps.content: Professor...
Linda's face has never seemed so somber.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: ...What happened?
When you're back at the Bureau, it's still well before dawn. You see a small shadow outside the main gate.
[Schorl] 1s
Before going to meet Celine, you ordered it to stay behind and forbade it from following. So it waited at the gate until now.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: You have not taken any alarming actions. There is no need for surveillance.
You say nothing and simply walk past it, entering through the main gate. Schorl follows.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: However, based on past experience, your current reaction is rather unusual. I believe you did not obtain the answers you wanted from Professor Fabius. That's why you're wandering around alone at night.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Based on past experience and online research, this may be defined as "loneliness." I believe you may need a companion.
You stop and turn back to look at it. It's still the same dull, black body, except now there's a scar on it. Seeing you turn around, it pauses for a moment.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Did I misjudge? Do I need to be recalibrated?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...No, you don't.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But now, I may take an alarming action.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Please state your request. I will assess it.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Calculation completed. Result: This is a high-risk action. Proceed with caution.
For some reason, even though it's still using the same brainwave communication, you can feel the signals becoming heavier.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Follow me.
